title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-24
notes:
West leads the ♦A against 3♣. After West cashes 3 rounds of diamonds and continues the suit, South should attempt to count the hand before playing from the dummy.

One of the defenders must have at least 5 hearts. West would have opened the bidding 1♥ if he had 5 hearts. Since East must have 5 hearts, he must, therefore, also have 5 spades. If East had less than 5 spades, he would have responded 1♥ not 1♠. East's shape is probably 5521 (6520 is also possible).

Discarding dummy's heart loser on the fourth diamond is unlikely to work as East will probably be able to ruff low. West will still have a trump trick. South should, therefore, ruff with the ♣10 and plan to squeeze East in the majors. East will have to have the ♥K, a card he has probably shown in the bidding and with his signal at trick 3.

A trick must be lost to the ♣Q. To retain a hand entry in clubs, which is necessary for the squeeze to function, South must duck either the first or the second round of clubs to West. Depending on which round of clubs is ducked and what suit West returns, a simple squeeze or a trump squeeze will develop against East.

Suppose West returns a trump after South ducks the first round of clubs. South can draw the last trump and cash another club pitching a heart from the dummy. East is trump squeezed. East must either bare his ♥K (South cashes the ♥A, ruffs the third spade, and scores the ♥Q) or come down to 3 spades (South ruffs out the spades and returns to the ♥A to cash the long spade).

If West had returned a heart after winning the ♣Q, South must win the ♥A. A trump squeeze is no longer possible. However, West's heart return has effectively performed a Vienna coup. East will be simple squeezed on the run of the clubs.
